authoredPrompt: This figure is a single-trace ultraviolet absorption spectrum of 1,3-butadiene plotted over a pink gradient field. The vertical axis is labeled "Absorbance", carries a magenta arrow pointing up beside the label, and runs from 0 to 1.0 with labeled ticks every 0.2. The horizontal axis reads "Wavelength (nm)", is followed by a magenta arrow pointing right, and spans 200 to 400 with labeled ticks every 20 nm. One magenta curve enters at the left edge near 0.34, climbs steeply to a rounded maximum just under 0.9 at about 215 nm, then falls sharply through 240 nm to roughly 0.07, after which it declines almost imperceptibly along a near-horizontal tail to about 0.03 at the right edge. A short annotation just above and right of the crest reads "lambda max = 217 nm". With the zero baseline at the bottom of the chart rather than the top, absorption registers as a peak rising off a flat floor, and the eye is meant to fix on that lone crest against the featureless tail beyond 250 nm. The trace records the wavelength of strongest absorption for a simple conjugated diene, the reading from which molar absorptivity is calculated.
authoredInteractions:
- Slider for wavelength: the learner scrubs from 200 to 400 nm, a dot rides the magenta curve with a live absorbance readout, making clear that lambda max is the wavelength where absorbance reaches its highest value.
- Toggle between peak-only and full-tail views: the figure alternately highlights the 217 nm crest and then the low absorbance tail beyond 250 nm, making clear that the diagnostic UV absorption for 1,3-butadiene is concentrated near the short-wavelength maximum.
authoredContext:
Note that UV spectra differ from IR spectra in how they are presented. For historical reasons, IR spectra are usually displayed so that the baseline corresponding to zero absorption runs across the top of the chart and a valley indicates an absorption, whereas UV spectra are displayed with the baseline at the bottom of the chart so that a peak indicates an absorption (the figure).

The ultraviolet spectrum of 1,3-butadiene, λmax = 217 nm.

The ultraviolet spectrum of 1,3-butadiene shows a peak at (217, 0.85) where lambda max equals 217 nanometers. The x-axis and y-axis represent wavelength and absorbance, respectively.

discrepancies: A magenta shaded fill under the curve from 200–250 nm (peakFill at 0.30 opacity) is shown in the default state; the source has no area fill, only a clean line over the pink gradient, so the default composition is altered.
The dynamic readout 'λ=217 nm, A=0.86' overlaps and collides with the static 'λ_max = 217 nm' annotation at the top of the plot, producing an unreadable jumble of two labels.
A filled dot plus a dashed vertical guide line at the peak are present by default; these interactive markers are absent from the source and add clutter to the step-0 view.
Because of the peak fill, the left shoulder of the crest reads as a solid pink blob rather than the source's thin magenta trace rising from ~0.34 at 200 nm.
